quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all controls are located before you ride.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Which organization certifies helmets for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: Choose a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for the best protection.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake. It does not give you more time to accelerate in curves.

questions.question: Riding a motorcycle is ______ driving a car.
questions.explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car, especially on long trips. Do not ride when you are tired. Fatigue reduces your control.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way
Speed up to put distance between you and them
Change lanes and let them pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Get the tailgater in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger and encourages them to follow faster.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?
questions.explanation: Engines seize when oil is low. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: In the left part of the lane, next to the centerline
In the right part of the lane, next to the curb
It depends on road and traffic conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Change your position as traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. A person's sex, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent maintenance than a car.
More frequent maintenance than a car.
Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent maintenance than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle often. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, whether or not there is a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross first. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly, then slowly add front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Be extra careful when approaching and riding through intersections.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Leave their blind spot as quickly as possible.
Slow down in the passing lane.
Not worry about your own blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave their blind spot as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Get out of another vehicle's blind spot quickly. Move into the passing lane and speed up to pass the vehicle.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that do not work properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, be especially careful of:

options.text: Drivers looking for a place to park.

questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, use caution. Vehicles may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handle grips.
Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handle grips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handle grips.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: Keeping space around your motorcycle is important because it:

options.text: Stops other vehicles from distracting you.
Gives you time to react to surprises.
Keeps traffic moving at the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired on a long ride, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you will feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down. Note that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive at this exact speed.
The highest legal speed is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive. In rain, snow, ice, or bad weather, you must drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.question: If you brake while turning:

options.text: You may have less grip as you lean.
You will have more grip as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Your traction is being used to make the turn while leaning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: When braking on slippery surfaces, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use caution and apply the brakes gently.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this intersection.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not protect as much as either of these.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms uncovered.
Shoes that do not cover the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Footwear should have low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Can you ride around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train sounds. It is illegal to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to get into a collision?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts with other traffic happen most often.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in the rain?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain begins. Ride in tire tracks left by cars for better grip.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a motorcycle horn?

options.text: Other people usually cannot hear it.
It can get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: A horn can help get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: How should you secure a load on your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Keep loads low to prevent upsetting your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: How should you approach angled railroad tracks?
questions.explanation: Simply go straight in your lane when crossing angled tracks. Turning to meet tracks at a right angle can push you into another lane.

questions.question: How should passengers hold on?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to grip your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They may also use secure handholds if available.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of an intersection ahead where a road joins from the right.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Only if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.
